title: Traffic Cadenza: policy compiler for staged rollouts with cohort-aware invariants
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Goal: Implement a policy compiler (Traffic Cadenza) that turns a high-level staged rollout specification into concrete, enforceable runtime rules for traffic splitting, cohort-targeting, step schedules, and automated rollback triggers. This ticket covers design, runtime hooks, telemetry contract, and migration for existing canary configs.

Background: Current rollout capabilities are fragmented: a mix of ad-hoc traffic split configs, manual step scripts, and several unsafe automatic rollbacks. We need a single declarative surface that: (1) is expressive for A/B, canary, and shadow strategies, (2) encodes safety invariants (latency/error budgets/degradation hysteresis), (3) compiles to deployment-ready routing policies compatible with hosted and Dedicated modes, and (4) supports gradual operator overrides and audit trails.

High-level proposal: Build a compiler that accepts a YAML/JSON DSL and emits: (A) a deterministic step schedule (time or observed-metric driven), (B) a set of runtime guards (threshold checks with windowing and hysteresis), (C) cohort routing maps for weighted splits including attribute-based cohorts, and (D) an auto-rollback policy with backoff and human-notify hooks. The compiler also produces a machine-readable audit summary and a human-friendly plan view for Console.

Core concepts in DSL (non-exhaustive):
- steps: ordered list with percent allocations and optional min-duration or metric-criteria
- cohorts: named selectors (region, vip, customer_segment) that can be targeted in any step
- invariants: latency_p50/latency_p95/error_rate/quality_score with window, comparator, and hysteresis
- probes: shadow or mirrored requests to gather probe metrics without impacting live traffic
- rollback_policy: immediate | delayed | graduated with cool-down and manual-confirmation flags
- observability_bindings: map of metrics and tracing spans to drive decisioning

Policy config example (DSL snippet):
---
strategy: staged
baseline_variant: v1.12
candidate_variant: v1.13
cohorts:
  - name: enterprise
    selector: { account_tier: "enterprise" }
  - name: eu
    selector: { region: "eu" }
steps:
  - name: step-1
    allocations: [{ variant: candidate, percent: 2, cohort: default }]
    min_duration: "PT30M"
  - name: step-2
    allocations: [{ variant: candidate, percent: 10, cohort: enterprise }, { variant: candidate, percent: 5, cohort: default }]
    metric_triggers:
      - name: p95-latency
        metric: request_latency_p95_ms
        comparator: <=
        threshold: 1200
        window: "5m"
rollback_policy:
  mode: graduated
  degrade_to: baseline
  cool_down: "PT15M"
  notify: ["#oncall", "pm@redwood.ai"]
---

Runtime semantics: The compiler emits a state machine where each step has an enter/exit predicate. Predicates are resolved either by wall-clock (min_duration elapsed) or by metric-derived success (all invariants satisfied for configured window). Guard evaluation runs in the routing control-plane and emits events: step_entered, step_paused, step_rolled_back, step_succeeded. Rollback has two flavors: automatic (triggered by invariant violation) and staged-revert (gradual percent reduction with verification). Hysteresis windows avoid flip-flopping on noisy signals.

Telemetry contract: Each policy must bind to a telemetry namespace and provide: request_volume, success_rate, error_rate_by_code, latency_p50/p95/p99, quality_regression_score, and sampled traces with variant tag. Compiler will also produce recommended alert queries and a small set of evaluation dashboards (Console manifests).

Acceptance criteria:
- DSL v1 parser + compiler emits state machine + JSON runtime policy
- Control-plane enforces traffic split atomically across candidate/baseline for a step
- Guards evaluate and trigger rollback with audit event + notification
- Shadow probe harness records results in a sandboxed metrics stream (no ingestion to customer-facing SLOs)
- Console shows the plan view and live step state with links to telemetry and PRs
- Migration: existing ad-hoc canary configs are importable via a compatibility helper

Implementation plan (phases):
1) Spec and DSL: finalize fields, invariants, and audit schema (owner: @ravi). (2 weeks)
2) Compiler MVP: parser + state machine emitter + unit tests. (3 weeks)
3) Control-plane hooks: runtime guard evaluator + atomic split applier + event bus. (4 weeks)
4) Console integration: plan visualization, manual override controls, audit timeline. (2 weeks)
5) Canary migration & ops playbook + runbook for oncall. (1 week)

Migration and compatibility: Provide a one-click importer that maps legacy traffic-split configs into the DSL with conservative defaults. Backfill historical telemetry pointers and mark compiled policies as "managed" so Console can switch between legacy and compiled paths.

Security & compliance: Compiler emits RBAC metadata for who can approve steps and who can initiate rollbacks. All audit events are forwarded to the customer audit log when running in Private/Dedicated modes.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Where to place the primary evaluation loop: control plane vs per-edge router? (Tentative: control plane for easier observability, with fast-path enforcement via edge admission tokens.)
- How expressive should cohort selectors be without opening explosion of routing table size? (We will support attribute selectors + sampling buckets; complex selectors compile to tag-based routing to keep tables bounded.)
- Auto-rollback aggressiveness vs false-positives: choose conservative defaults and provide operator knob.

Docs & links:
- RFC: https://docs.internal.redwood.ai/rfcs/traffic-cadenza
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/6821
- Console concept mocks: https://drive.google.com/traffic-cadenza-mocks

Risks / mitigation:
- Risk: noisy signals causing unnecessary rollbacks. Mitigation: hysteresis windows, multi-metric voting, and decaying confidence.
- Risk: routing table blowup. Mitigation: cohort compaction and tag-based routing emitter.

Next steps:
- Sync with SRE to finalize telemetry namespaces (blocking until 2025-02-12)
- Design review with Console PM to finalize plan UI (target 2025-02-18)
- Begin Compiler MVP implementation after spec sign-off
acceptance_test_plan:
1) Unit tests for DSL parsing and state machine emission.
2) Integration test: deploy a fake variant with synthetic metrics and verify step transitions and rollback.
3) E2E on staging: import 3 legacy canaries, run staged rollout with shadow probes, assert no customer-facing errors, and verify audit events.
4) Load test: ensure route table size growth < 5% for 10k cohorts when compiled via compaction algorithm.
migration_notes: Compatibility importer will map legacy keys: legacy.percent -> steps[0].allocations, legacy.shadow -> probes, legacy.watchers -> invariants. We will tag imported policies with "imported_legacy:true" and default rollback_policy to "graduated". Ops will run importer in read-only dry-run first.
